messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] procD.lm() function
parts:
Nicole,

You are using type I (sequential) sums of squares and cross-products.  With Type I SSCP, order matters.  Neither is correct nor incorrect - it depnds on how you define the order.  

If you want results that are the same, no matter the order, you could consider type III SSCP (change the SS.type argument).

Cheers!
Mike

messages.author: 96a78639336ed702
messages.subject: Re: procD.lm() function
parts:
Hello Nicole,

The different outputs results from your choice of sum of squares and cross-products (SSCP), SS in short. 

SS comes in three types, Type I, Type II, and Type III.

For Type I SS, each term in the model is estimated in light of all terms preceding it (This is why Type I SS is call "sequential" SS ). For size*sex, the effect of size is estimated first. When estimating the effect of sex, the effect of size is taken into consideration. When estimating the effect of the interaction term size:sex, the effect of both size and sex are taken into consideration. For sex*size, the effect of sex is estimated first. When estimating the effect of size, the effect of sex is taken into consideration. When estimating the effect of the interaction term size:sex, the effect of both size and sex are taken into consideration. The procD.lm function defaults to Type I SS. So you observed different main effect of size and sex in mode 1 and model 2. But note that both models yielded the same effect for the interaction term since its effect is estimated in light of the effect of both size and sex in both models.


For Type II SS, a main effect is estimated in light of all other main effects, without regard to the interaction term. 

model3 <- procD.lm(coords ~ size*sex, iter = 9999, SS.type = "II", data = gdf)
model4 <- procD.lm(coords ~ sex*size, iter = 9999, SS.type = "II", data = gdf)

In both model3 and model 4, estimates for size, sex, and size:sex will be the same. The effect of size is always estimated in light of the effect of sex, and vice versa. The effect of size:sex is estimated in light of both the effect of size and sex. It is essentially the same as the estimates for the interaction term you obtained in model 1 and model 2.


For Type III SS, the effect of any term is estimated in light of the effect of all other terms. 

model5 <- procD.lm(coords ~ size*sex, iter = 9999, SS.type = "III", data = gdf)
model6 <- procD.lm(coords ~ sex*size, iter = 9999, SS.type = "III", data = gdf)

In both model5 and model6, the effect of size is estimated in light of the effect of sex and size:sex. The effect of sex is estimated in light of the effect of size and size:sex. The effect of size:sex is estimated in light of the effect of size and sex. Changing the order of main effect again doesn't affect the estimates for any term.


According to your statement, there seemed to be no particular reason to believe the order of size and sex in the model to be important. Therefore, Type II or III may be more appropriate. The choice between the two depends on whether you would like to account for the effect of interaction term when estimating main effects. If yes, choose Type III; if no, choose Type II.


Regards,
Patrick
